title: Automated Testing in CI
subtitle: Run unit tests, integration tests, upload coverage, and fail the pipeline on regressions

content.text: Running tests in CI — the complete setup

content.code:
name: Tests
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci

      # Run tests with coverage
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: npm test -- --coverage --coverageReporters=json-summary --coverageReporters=lcov

      # Upload coverage to Codecov (free for open source)
      - name: Upload to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ./coverage/lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: true

      # Upload coverage report as artifact
      - name: Archive coverage
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: coverage-report
          path: coverage/
          retention-days: 7

  integration-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Start a PostgreSQL service container alongside the test runner
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: testpass
          POSTGRES_DB: testdb
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci

      - name: Run integration tests
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:testpass@localhost:5432/testdb
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
        run: npm run test:integration

# In package.json / vitest.config.ts:
# coverage: { thresholds: { lines: 80, functions: 80, branches: 70 } }
# Test command fails with non-zero exit if thresholds aren't met

# In workflow:
- name: Test with coverage check
  run: npm test -- --coverage
  # Exits 1 if below threshold → step fails → job fails → PR is blocked

# For a more nuanced approach: check the JSON summary in the workflow
- name: Check coverage threshold
  run: |
    COVERAGE=$(node -e "const c = require('./coverage/coverage-summary.json'); \
      console.log(c.total.lines.pct)")
    echo "Line coverage: $COVERAGE%"
    node -e "if ($COVERAGE < 80) { console.error('Coverage below 80%!'); process.exit(1); }"

content.filename: Test reporters for GitHub PR annotations
content.code:
- name: Run tests
  run: npm test -- --reporter=json --outputFile=test-results.json

# Publish test results as PR check with inline annotations
- name: Publish test results
  uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1
  if: always()   # run even if tests fail
  with:
    name: Test Results
    path: test-results.json
    reporter: jest-json
    # Now failing tests show as inline PR annotations
    # and a 'Test Results' check appears in the PR

content.text: Use if: always() for artifact uploads and reports. By default, later steps are skipped if an earlier step fails. But you want to upload test results even when tests fail — that's exactly when you need the report. Adding if: always() to the upload step ensures it runs regardless of test outcome.

questions.question: Your integration tests need a PostgreSQL database. What is the cleanest way to provide it in GitHub Actions?
options: Install PostgreSQL with apt-get in a run step
Use 'services:' in the job definition — GitHub spins up a postgres service container alongside the runner
Connect to a shared test database hosted externally
Mock all database calls so no real database is needed
questions.explanation: GitHub Actions 'services:' runs Docker containers alongside the runner for the duration of the job. They're configured with health checks so your tests don't start until the database is ready. They use the same network as the runner, so you connect at localhost. This is the cleanest, most isolated approach — no external dependencies, no cleanup needed.

faq.q: Should I run tests on every commit or only on PRs?
faq.a: Both. Run a fast subset (unit tests only, ~30s) on every push to any branch — instant feedback. Run the full suite including integration and E2E tests on PRs targeting main — thorough validation before merge. This gives speed on developer branches and safety before merging.

examples: Codecov integrates with GitHub PRs to show coverage change per file: '+2.3% coverage' or '-1.1% coverage' as a PR comment — makes coverage visible in code review
Services containers eliminate the 'but my local DB has different data' problem — every CI run starts with a clean, identical database
